## Lists...
Prove that lists can have anything

```{r}

l = list(
  vec_numeric = 5:17,
  mat = matrix(1:8, nrow = 2, ncol = 4, byrow = TRUE),
  vec_logical = c(TRUE),
  summary_table = summary(rnorm(1000)))

l

l[[1]]
#$ is a shorthand for double brackets
l[[2]]
l[["vec_logical"]]
```


## 'for' loops

```{r}
list_norm = list(
  a = rnorm(20, 3, 4),
  b = rnorm(20, -14, 20),
  c = rnorm(20, 1000, 1000),
  d = rnorm(20, 0, 1)
)
list_norm 
```

Can I get mean and sd for each sample


```{r}
source("source_mean_sd.R")
```


```{r}
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[1]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[2]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[3]])
mean_and_sd(list_norm[[4]])
```

Can I do this better?
```{r}
output = vector("list", length = 4)
for(i in 1:4) {
  output[[i]] = mean_and_sd(list_norm[[i]])
}
output
```

## 'map' instead
1. Take for loop and modify to make logic a little more clear
2. eventually take statements and build them into tidyverse operations

This is bettter:
```{r}
output = map(list_norm, mean_and_sd)

output_2 = map(list_norm, IQR)

output
output_2
```
output - place we're going to save it
list_norm = list input
mean_and_sd = function to apply to list


# What about map variants

```{r}
output_3 = map_df(list_norm, mean_and_sd)
output_4 = map_dbl(list_norm, median)

output_3
output_4
```
way to simplify output

map_dbl = just collapsing everything to a simple output structure
  -regular map always gives you a list
  -this just gives you a vector

## List columns

Time to make list columns
```{r}
listcol_df = 
  tibble(
    name = c("a", "b", "c", "d"),
    samp = list_norm
  )
listcol_df
```
named list column: collection of 20 numbers for samp 1

Do stuff with this

```{r}
listcol_df |> 
  filter(name %in% c("a", "b", "c"))

listcol_df |> 
  pull(samp)
```

What about mean and sd
```{r}
mean_and_sd(pull(listcol_df, samp)[[1]])
```

Can I iterate?
```{r}
map(pull(listcol_df, samp), mean_and_sd)
```

This is where it gets really cool
Apply sd to each of these thigns and save the results:
```{r}
listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map(samp, mean_and_sd)
  )

listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map_df(samp, mean_and_sd)
  )

listcol_df |> 
  mutate(
    output = map_dbl(samp, mean_and_sd[[1]])
  )
```

## Another example

NSDUH import etc

```{r}
source("nsduh_process.R")
```

```{r}
nsduh_url = "https://www.samhsa.gov/data/sites/default/files/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015/NSDUHsaeShortTermCHG2015.htm"

nsduh_html = read_html(nsduh_url)

nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = 1)
nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = 4)
nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = 5)
```

import using iteration

```{r}

output = vector("list", length = 3)

table_num = c(1,4,5)

for (i in 1:3) {
  output [[i]] = nsduh_process(html = nsduh_html, table_num = table_num[i])
}
```


let's build up a map example
```{r}
map(table_num, nsduh_process, html = nsduh_html)
```


Lets try list columns
```{r}

nsduh_df = 
  tibble(
    drug = c("marj", "cocaine", "heroin"),
    num = c(1, 4, 5)
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    table = map(num, nsduh_process, html = nsduh_html)
  ) |> 
  select(-num) |> 
  unnest(table)

nsduh_df |> 
  filter(age == "12-17", ) |> 
  mutate(State = fct_reorder(State, percent)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = State, y = percent, color = year)) +
  geom_point() +
  facet_grid(. ~ drug)

nsduh_df 
```
before unnest have data frame: 3 rows: drug and full table imported, etc
unnest - can unnest and expand those

## Weather again

```{r}
data("weather_df")

weather_df = 
  weather_df |> 
  nest(data = date:tmin)
```


Why would you want to do that:
suppose you want regress: tmax vs tmin: way to do that:
```{r}
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[1]])
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[2]])
lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = pull(weather_df, data)[[3]])

weather_lm = function(input_data) {
  
  lm(tmax ~ tmin, data = input_data)
}
weather_lm(pull(weather_df, data)[[1]])

weather_df |> 
  mutate(lm_fits = map(data, weather_lm)
         ) |> 
  pull(lm_fits)
```
linear regression model that pulls tmax vs tmin for model dataset: function takes entire dataset and gives data set that fits the model

Applying that function to this dataset and apply to each of the datasets

If want to fit linear model to each column of weather dataframe. Going to mutate to use function to each col of data frame. Add column right next to it to compare side by side

Function simplifies this output: just using lm is complicated but just having one input will simplify and result in a function 

If you want to keep track of data with each center, need to use this function.
